facts.fact: Marketing attribution models generally fall into two categories: single-touch and multi-touch.
facts.quote: Marketing attribution models generally fall into two categories: **single-touch** and **multi-touch**.

facts.fact: First-touch attribution gives all the credit to the first marketing interaction a customer has with a brand.
facts.quote: first-touch attribution is a single-touch model that gives all the credit to the first marketing interaction a customer has with your brand

facts.fact: Linear attribution gives every touch point in the customer journey equal credit for a conversion.
facts.quote: Linear attribution gives every touch point in the customer journey equal credit for a conversion.

facts.fact: Time-decay attribution gives more credit to interactions that occur closer to the conversion.
facts.quote: gives more credit to the interactions that occur closer to the conversion, while earlier interactions are weighted less heavily

facts.fact: Position-based attribution gives more weight to the first interactions at the top of the funnel and the last interactions before conversion, distributing remaining credit across the points in between.
facts.quote: gives more weight to specific stages of the customer journey—namely, the first interactions at the top of the funnel and the last interactions before conversion

facts.fact: Data-driven attribution uses algorithms and customer journey data to determine how much credit different marketing activities receive for a conversion, rather than a predefined formula.
facts.quote: Data-driven attribution uses algorithms and customer journey data to determine how much credit different marketing activities should receive for a conversion.
